citation.quote: Typically, the wood fences were constructed as post and rail, post and board, or Virginia worm. A few stone walls could also be found on the property (see Buildings and Structures). Some were dismantled before the fighting began on July 2 to allow ease of troop movement, while the wooden rails were used to create new breastworks. Other fences were left partially or wholly standing, because they did not impede troop movement, they were out of the line of the battle, or they were left as obstacles for the advancing enemy.
